title: AMECEA PLENARY: AMECEA Bishops End 21st Plenary with Call for Partnership in Youth Ministry
desc:
Sr. Jecinter Antoinette Okoth, FSSA
At the close of the eight-day Plenary Assembly for the Bishops of the Association of Member Episcopal Conferences in Eastern Africa (AMECEA), the Church leaders have appealed for partnership from all sectors, including Catholics, governments, political leaders, and people of goodwill, in accompanying the young people in the region.
Reading the statement on behalf of the Bishops on Sunday, July 26, Rt. Rev. Martin Mtumbua of Karonga Diocese, Malawi, stressed the need for different sectors of society to play their part in supporting youth as active partners in both Church and public life.
Addressing Catholics across the Eastern Africa region, the bishops urged the faithful to welcome young people as genuine partners in mission. They called for parishes, Small Christian Communities, and diocesan structures to be more open to youth voice and leadership, paired with steady, Christ-centered catechesis shaped by Catholic Social Teaching.
To the governments and public authorities, the Church leaders appealed for policies that protect human dignity and widen access to education. They also called for conditions that support entrepreneurship, decent work, safe migration, and civic participation among young people, alongside greater political will to resolve conflicts through dialogue.
[caption id=attachment_25245 align=alignright width=300] Bishop Mtumbuka[/caption]
The Sunday communique also addressed political leaders, reminding them that young people raised concerns about being used during election campaigns and forgotten after elections. They described this as a call to “conscience,” and insisted on an end to the exploitation of youth for political gain. The Bishops therefore invited political leaders to become models who inspire hope.
Beyond the Church partners, Eastern Africa Church leaders addressed ecumenical, interreligious, corporate, and development partners, inviting them to help build the pastoral, psycho-social, educational, and digital structures needed for young people to thrive.
Pointing out that the youth are not only the future of the Church and society but already its present, the Bishops echoed Saint Paul's message to Timothy that young people should not let anyone “look down on them because of their youth, but be an example in speech, conduct, love, faith, and purity.”
The bishops also invited young people, in the spirit of synodality, to walk with Jesus as the disciples did on the road to Emmaus, to let their hearts burn as the Scriptures are opened to them, to recognize the Lord in the breaking of the bread, and then to rise and share what they have seen and heard, walking together with their Bishops.
The Bishops therefore invited all people of goodwill to pray and cooperate with the Church on behalf of the region's young people, so that together they might build bridges of communion, hope, justice, and good governance.

title: A graphene-based intelligent reconfigurable reflective surface for circularly polarized beam scanning in 6G applications
desc: This paper presents a graphene-based reconfigurable intelligent surface (CP-GRIS) for circularly polarized beam scanning in the sub-THz range. The 1-bit coding metasurface combines phase tuning and polarization conversion in a compact structure, enabling dynamic beam steering with low sidelobe levels. The structure consists of a 45 $$\times$$ 45 array ($$15 \lambda \times 15 \lambda$$) of unit cells, each formed by two inverted semilunar-shaped gold patches and an embedded graphene strip that produces a controllable $$180^\circ$$ phase difference via current reversal. This phase control yields two stable phase states with an approximately $$180^\circ$$ phase difference over 266-332 GHz, while maintaining a reflection magnitude above 0.85. By modulating graphene’s chemical potential and thereby altering its surface conductivity, the metasurface switches between these two stable phase states. This reconfigurability enables the reported single-beam operation and full two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) beam-scanning capability. At 300 GHz, the proposed CP-GRIS achieves a maximum broadside gain of 24.8 dBi, a beamwidth of $$4.4^\circ$$. The proposed RIS achieves beam steering with a sidelobe level 15.3 dB below the main lobe at broadside, primarily due to its large electrical aperture and phase-controlled 1-bit coding, resulting in a gain enhancement of 12.4 dBi over the feed horn antenna. Beam scanning up to $$\pm 40^\circ$$ is achieved with a low scan loss of 1.2 dBi, highlighting the proposed CP-GRIS as an efficient and versatile platform for sub-THz and THz beam manipulation and emerging sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems.

title: Slovenia's Tadej Pogacar wins record-tying 5th Tour de France title
desc: Tadej Pogacar won a record-equaling fifth Tour de France title on Sunday. The 27-year-old Slovenian dominated this year's race to join Belgian Eddy Merckx, Spaniard Miguel Indurain and Frenchmen Jacques Anquetil and Bernard Hinault as the only riders to win five Tours.
